phases.note: M0156 pre-registered, run at five widths, read on both histories, written verdict. Two dated CSVs + a plain-language record under docs/lab/survivorship/. No engine module edited, no roster entry touched, no migration written. THE ANSWER IS TWENTY by the pre-registered rule, not judgement: narrowest rung at or under 23.0% on the honest history -- twenty clears at 20.08% and is also best on return (12.46%/yr) and MAR (0.621). Widening costs 1.7 pts/yr and buys 1.5 pts of fall. THE MECHANISM IS DATED: four of five widths trough in August 1998, a market-wide month; the OTHER roster book's worst at twenty was spring 2006, a single-name accident in a rising market. Width fixes the second kind and not the first, so the two books want different widths for a reason you can point at on a calendar. Confirming detail: 2006 is the one stretch where width visibly works here (14.3% at twenty -> 9.9% at forty-five) but 2006 was never THIS book's worst episode -- which is also why twenty-FIVE reads worse than twenty: widening shaved 2006 just enough to leave 1998 standing alone. 25% BAR NOT BREACHED (20.08%) so the state-it-at-the-top branch never fired; the reassuring finding is primary throughout. TWO OWN PREDICTIONS RECORDED AS WRONG rather than dropped. DECISIONS: (a) rung 1 split hold B into B1/B2, prose written unlocked between. (b) did NOT run lab reevaluate -- it had already run at 71bbf22 after all four ids left idea; invariant 13 says ONCE not four times, and lab note changes no trial/status/N so its input was unchanged. The literal self-check would have returned true, but it exists to find the one session that CLOSES the batch and phase 5 was that session. Good judgement over literal reading. (c) kept both CSVs -- raw grid carries PF/Sharpe/DSR inputs/reproduction flags, era grid carries trough dates, neither a superset. (d) narrowed the era caveat to the measured scope. VERIFICATION: ruff clean; 4992 passed 3 skipped (opt-in live-store only, no DB skip, PG_TEST_URL exported); 4 test looks before and after; grid.csv byte-identical to 661870d; snapshot byte-compare green with the pair clean at HEAD; nothing of a peer's swept in. HANDOVER ITEM, NOT ACTED ON: CLAUDE.md line 80 still states the real-money bar as 'max DD <= 20%', but design doc line 20 and section 18 record the owner revising condition 4 to <= 25% on 2026-10-14 with his words quoted. CLAUDE.md is one dated revision behind; anyone reading it alone would mis-grade both roster books including phase 2's 35-name entry. Phase 1 used 25% correctly because the dated owner revision governs. FOLLOW-UP correctly scoped out: lab exposure M0156 reads most of it free and would settle whether the book's own safety rule already absorbs the single-name damage width would otherwise absorb.

phases.note: M0155 REJECTED -- 'the brake sells companies the book never owned'. Four commits: fa67e5a pre-registration, fb3f848 run + check-store read, 01efde8 dated era grid and report, 280923e verdict. A CLEAN NULL and the mechanism is worth more than the number: all six arms leave the spring-2006 fall at 21.83% on the honest tape, identical to the unbraked book to FOUR DECIMAL PLACES; five of six identical on every era column on both stores. No cost either -- returns within a third of a point, trades within 13 of 1640. It does not close the hole, does not cost anything, and is not width in disguise: it is not width at all. WHY: the brake fires on 135 of 175 monthly decisions and named 820 companies in twenty years; THE BOOK HELD ELEVEN. In spring 2006 it named 36 and held NONE. A momentum host ranks on twelve months of past return and buys the top twenty; a name two standard deviations behind the index over a quarter is already out of that twenty by construction. The two screens read opposite ends of the same list. LAB-LEVEL FINDING: a per-holding relative-shortfall brake on a momentum book is near-inert BY CONSTRUCTION -- this should stop the next person proposing the shape unless the host picks on something other than past return. *** DUPLICATE REEVALUATE RACE, resolved exactly as designed: BOTH phase 5 and phase 3 ran the invariant-13 check, both legitimately saw all four ids off idea, and both ran lab reevaluate. Phase 5 ran first at 71bbf22 and 1 method moved (M0086). Phase 3 ran second, got 0 method(s) moved, the pair still matched HEAD, and so committed NOTHING -- which is precisely the plan's specified behaviour. The lock serialised them and the second run was a no-op, so the race was self-correcting and cost nothing. No double-counting of N. *** STATUS-vs-VERDICT FLAG, not a contradiction: M0155's recorded STATUS is dev-eligible while the verdict says rejected. The status is the mechanical dev screen; the hypothesis pre-committed BEFORE the run that an eligible read on this line is a by-product that must not be reported as a candidate or a near miss, because promotion is refused on kin whatever it scores. The status was not forced -- the lab is append-only and records what the screen said, while the verdict carries the judgement. Changing the roster-facing view so an inert method does not show as dev-eligible is a SEPARATE argued change, correctly not made unasked. VERIFICATION: 4 test looks before and after, confirmed twice; grid.csv byte-identical to 661870d; git diff 661870d over the methods directory shows ONLY the four NEW files, so no frozen method moved; ruff clean; full suite running in a DETACHED WORKTREE at origin/main so peers' uncommitted edits cannot confuse the read -- number to follow rather than claimed early. LOCK DISCIPLINE: two holds, 4m35s and 1m25s, six minutes total against a plan that budgeted one hold spanning the whole phase; the era grid's 26 backtests, the report prose and the overlap diagnostic all ran outside it. NOTE: task id is P2-ENG-N60A, not the P1-ENG-W35C the sibling naming would suggest.

An account-reading brake escapes the behaviour rule a market-reading brake cannot; measured, not argued. Texture: against two of the four failed books the control reads 0.359/0.343 and the drawdown-braked arms 0.625/0.631 -- account-reading brakes cost about half the distance to the line, market-reading brakes cost all of it. COST: every brake works and every one is paid out of the return. Worst fall 68.7%->19.3-33.2%; funded return 9.9%->5.9-9.2% vs SPY TR 7.2%. The only arm keeping half the +2.7pt lead (loose vol dial, 9.2%) still falls 33.2%; both arms inside the 25% bar lose to the index outright. A recovery cost not a crash cost -- the drawdown brake turned a 23%/yr 2009-2015 stretch into 12.9%/yr. All six failed DSR>=0.90 (0.51-0.67 at N=95), 0 of 4 folds. Residue worth keeping: the volatility dial beat the drawdown dial on every axis at once. phases.note: M0148 REJECTED DIRECTION, the rare clean kind -- lost return AND safety at once, nothing to trade off. wait none 11.3%/20.4%/+4.1 SPY lead; 1 check 10.2/20.4/+3.0; 2 checks 9.8/25.3/+2.6; 3 checks 9.0/31.6/+1.8; 3 sell-only 10.0/31.4/+2.9. Monotone decay in return and the worst fall goes the WRONG way, 20->32%. A brake that deepens the drawdown is not a brake. ANCHOR HELD IN THE RECORDED PATH, not just the pre-check: M0148-K0 vs trial n=467 identical to the digit on start, end, trades 575, max_drawdown, cagr, profit_factor, exposure, turnover. ONLY dsr differs (0.943236881080622 vs M0143's 0.941320611624543) and that is CORRECT not a miss -- DSR is scored at its run-date N and N moved since M0143 ran. NOT A NULL: the cool-off genuinely bound, 8/14/24/15 refused moves over 238 checks, turnover 5.37->5.03, switch 31 changes of mind -> 23. The idea got a real chance and was refused on its merits. WHERE THE MONEY WENT -- 2008: the book beat the market by 35.7% that year with the switch free and by only 27-28% in every version that made it wait. The suppressed flips were not whipsaw, they were the exit the switch exists for; at three checks it was blocked from selling in May/June/July 2008 and from buying back through three straight months of the 2003 recovery. Chop years never improved: 2009-2015 reads -0.5% with no lock and -1.4/-0.6/-1.0/-0.0 with it, AND the binds do not match the story -- clustered in 2011 and early 2012, none in 2010, none in 2015, said so in the verdict rather than letting the three-year framing stand. Kin clean PER VARIANT not just the best twin: max 0.7292 against the 0.85 bar, all five arms against all four test-failed books. *** LABEL CAVEAT, stated in the verdict and the commit so nobody misreads the lab: M0148 records as dev-eligible, but that is the CONTROL arm -- the existing switch re-run unchanged. NONE of the four arms carrying the idea cleared the screen, and the method lost most of its walk-forward folds. *** INVARIANT 13: the check said it WAS last (M0148 dev-eligible, M0149 rejected, M0155 dev-eligible, M0156 rejected -- all four off idea), ran reevaluate inside the same hold, 1 method moved (M0086 rejected->dev-eligible at N=98), ran a second time as a settle check, 0 moved. EXIT CRITERIA ALL GREEN: pair clean vs HEAD, grid.csv byte-identical to 661870d, 4 test looks before and after (491 dev trials), no lab test and no --store at .research-test anywhere, ruff clean, 995 tests pass across test_m0148/test_lab_methods/test_lab_snapshot INCLUDING test_the_committed_snapshot_is_the_export_of_the_committed_database which was red earlier in the set and is now green.
